### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**29** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b51ec5777a46be8f74a4df48c1b7eaf8268e8ea8` — the merge of head `d7dd7d7b1333eae9a128ba36a960735ebb9f595e` into base `82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b51ec5777a46be8f74a4df48c1b7eaf8268e8ea8 && git checkout b51ec5777a46be8f74a4df48c1b7eaf8268e8ea8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 d7dd7d7b1333eae9a128ba36a960735ebb9f595e && git checkout -B drift-repro 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 && git merge --no-ff d7dd7d7b1333eae9a128ba36a960735ebb9f595e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d7dd7d7b1333eae9a128ba36a960735ebb9f595e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-diff-delete-load.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-stored-expression-fill.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/objectql/src/stored-expression-backfill.test.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.test.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json, content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx, .changeset/32958-delete-extension-fill-stored-expressions.md (read: packages/objectql/src/stored-expression-backfill.ts captureStoredExpressions / changedSince)

Face: schema (a `packages/spec/src/**` hit). Diff read against merge base `199e3624`. PR is `Part of #32958`; the card's second item (prose in `protocol-registry-hydration.ts`) is deliberately left out.

### ① Derived judgments

- The delete door now runs the one fill path (`captureStoredExpressionChange` → `fillStoredExpressionChange`) the save, publish, rollback and revert doors run. The capture is taken only for `targetState === 'active'`, before `restoreArtifactRegistryView`. The fill runs after the audit row, projector and mutation event, before the answer, which is the save door's order. A draft discard captures nothing.
- `filledObjectOf` keys `object_extension` by the object it extends, so `name` is the right object. A deleted `object` with nothing beneath it serves no fields afterwards: `changedSince(before, undefined)` is empty, so no row is read (checked in `stored-expression-backfill.ts`). This matches the new comment.
- `advisories` is spread only when non-empty, so a clean delete's bytes are unchanged. The fill never throws into the delete (`fillStoredExpressionChange` reports instead).
- The pins cover both save orders (object then extension, extension then object) with a red-on-main premise, a non-stored extension (no rows written, no key), a draft discard, and a schema round-trip of the produced answer through `DeleteMetaItemResponseSchema.parse`. The spec test flips the old "declares neither" pin to "does not declare `version`" plus a positive `advisories` pin.
- CI on this head was still running at review time (16 success, 9 skipped, 20 in progress, none failed). Landing needs all checks green on this head, which this record does not replace.

### ② Semver level

The changeset declares `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (a new optional response key) and `Metadata-protocol: added`. `@objectstack/spec` is `minor` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` is `patch`. That meets the gate's rule (a declared kind grades at least one moved package `minor`) and AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3. No ADR-0087 marker is owed for a widening. The authorable-surface baseline and the reference doc are regenerated in the same PR.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No governed path. The PR is authored by `objectstack-fleet[bot]` on the relay.
- N1 (nit): `filledObjectOf` also answers for type `object`, so deleting the stored row of an artifact-backed `object` now fills too, when the restored artifact definition changes a stored expression. That is correct and consistent with the save door, but the changeset and the schema description name only the `object_extension` case, and there is no pin for it. One sentence, and optionally one `it`, would cover it.
- N2 (nit): the `DeleteMetaItemResponseSchema` docblock says `advisories` comes "on the repository path's row-deleted return alone". Accurate for this head. If another delete branch ever gains a fill, that sentence needs to move with it.

### ④ Design judgment

`protocol.zod.ts`: the new optional `advisories` reuses `RuntimeAuthoringIssueSchema`, the save answer's element shape, with the same omitted-when-empty discipline. A client that ignores the key behaves as before, and `z.object` strips nothing it did not already strip. The rewritten docblock keeps the declared-equals-returned discipline. It still refuses `version` with its reason, and it says plainly that `advisories` carries no #4463 gate finding, only the fill. The first consumer (the delete door) emits exactly that shape, pinned through `parse`. The implementing files agree with the contract. No must-fix or should-fix; N1–N2 are nits. This is the final round.
